args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the v2.3.1 deploy, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. The SRE agent rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and look into why a release that failed in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

- **Cause:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run it, health checks pass, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Because v2.3.0 had been healthy in production before, this didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Incident:** I opened **INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, and it paged the on-call engineer. It explains what failed, the rollback, and the next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and look at why it reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.
